beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier while a compact DQ-CTM process repeatedly updates it before decoding.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: ThinkSR keeps the super-resolution field dense while the thought process stays compact. The encoder turns the low-resolution input into features. Windowing groups those features for the thought process without dropping the dense carrier. DQ-CTM runs repeated ticks with shared parameters. The decoder turns the updated carrier back into the super-resolution output.

params.headline: ThinkSR runs dense features through shared thought ticks
params.note: The recurrence belongs to the thought stage.

beats.intent: The carrier equation defines a dense feature field from the low-resolution image, then partitions that field into windows while preserving the tokens.
beats.narration: The method first names the persistent dense carrier. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into that feature field. The low-resolution image is the input being lifted into features. The window partition acts on the full carrier, so the token set comes from the dense field.

params.headline: The dense carrier is encoded before it is windowed

terms.label: Window partition keeps the carrier tokens

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the benchmark; at 1.129 million parameters, it is the second largest of the five methods.
beats.claim: ×4 lightweight super-resolution, average over five benchmarks.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison should not make DQ-CTM-SR sound cheap. CATANet is the smallest reported method at 0.535 million parameters. RFDN and IMDN remain below one million parameters. DQ-CTM-SR has 1.129 million parameters, making it the second largest of the five. CARN is larger at 1.592 million parameters.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is the second largest model in this table
params.note: Smallest first; values are parameter counts in millions.
